subject.title: Context pruning mode 'off' not preventing compactions (Anthropic API key, cache-ttl smart defaults)

question: Should OpenClaw add a supported hard-limit-only or fully-off automatic compaction mode, and should compaction entries persist a closed trigger reason for future triage?
rationale: Current main already honors pruning off, but the remaining request changes compaction safety semantics and transcript metadata, which is a compatibility-sensitive product choice rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Define hard-limit semantics
options.body: Add an approved config contract that preserves overflow recovery while disabling threshold/safeguard compaction, with docs, tests, and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Keep current compaction policy
options.body: Close the disable-mode portion as unsupported and limit follow-up work to verified false low-context trigger fixes and clearer docs.

options.title: Wait for narrower proof
options.body: Require current-main live Anthropic evidence before accepting a new compaction contract beyond the related sessions_yield report.

recommendation.title: Define hard-limit semantics
recommendation.body: Add an approved config contract that preserves overflow recovery while disabling threshold/safeguard compaction, with docs, tests, and upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The current-main blame and recent history put this owner closest to the compaction/pruning runtime boundary that needs the product decision.
